Findings:

1. (factual, BLOCKING) Melbourne 1880 Theme cell omits source text.

The staged row has Theme = `Arts, Manufactures and Agricultural and Industrial Products`, but the registered master `World's fair` World Expos table gives `Arts, Manufactures and Agricultural and Industrial Products of all Nations` for the 1880 Melbourne row. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World%27s_fair, World Expos table, line 277.

Minimal fix: update CSV row `(1880, Melbourne)` Theme to `Arts, Manufactures and Agricultural and Industrial Products of all Nations`, and update any curation universe_listing / examples that repeat the shorter value.

2. (factual, BLOCKING) Three Country cells do not match the visible Location country text in the registered master table.

The schema says `Country`, and source_coverage says this is supplied by the master table's Location cell. A parse of the visible World Expos table yields these Location countries:
- 1929 Barcelona: `Spain`, but CSV stages `Restoration (Spain)`. Source: World Expos table, line 289.
- 1937 Paris: `France`, but CSV stages `French Third Republic`. Source: World Expos table, line 292.
- 1949 Port-au-Prince: `Haiti`, but CSV stages `Republic of Haiti (1859–1957)`. Source: World Expos table, line 294.

The staged values appear to come from flag-icon alt/link context rather than the visible Location cell. That is not consistently applied across the table: earlier French/Spanish/UK rows use the visible modern country text rather than flag-era alt labels. With the current `Country` column name and source_count=1 table-value rule, these three cells should match the visible Location country text.

Minimal fix: change those Country cells to `Spain`, `France`, and `Haiti`, or else explicitly redefine the column as a period-state/flag-label extraction and apply that rule consistently across all 36 rows. The simpler repair is to use the visible table country text.

3. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) Active prose overstates the period-accurate-country rule.

Several draft/curation fields claim period-accurate country forms are preserved for five historical rows, including Restoration Spain, French Third Republic, and Republic of Haiti. Given Finding 2, that active prose will be stale after the simpler source-verbatim repair. It also already conflicts with the mixed extraction rule: some other rows with period flag context, such as 1888 Barcelona and 1889 Paris, are staged as `Spain` / `France`.

Minimal fix: revise temporal_note, _extraction_notes, collection_summary, decision_log, normalization_decisions, and universe_listing notes so the Country rule is `visible Location country text from the master table`; keep only Austria-Hungary and Colony of Victoria as visible table country forms if those remain unchanged.
